title: Resize to a chosen size
summary: Resizing changes image dimensions. OpenCV resize takes the target size as width, height, unlike the row-first array shape.
introduction: Resizing changes image dimensions. OpenCV resize takes the target size as width, height, unlike the row-first array shape. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain resize to a chosen size
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Resizing changes image dimensions. OpenCV resize takes the target size as width, height, unlike the row-first array shape.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

image = np.zeros((4, 6, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
small = cv2.resize(image, (3, 2), interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST)
print(small.shape)
blocks.title: Resize to a chosen size

blocks.text: The output is (2, 3, 3). The requested width is 3 and height is 2. Nearest-neighbour resizing selects nearby pixel values.

blocks.text: Changing width and height by different factors can stretch the picture.
